attacks.why: A jump whose target is past the end of the instruction array. On a real machine this is how you make execution continue into data you control.
attacks.detail: main[2] GOTO: jump target 9999 is outside the code (0..4)

attacks.why: ADD is executed with nothing on the stack. An unchecked stack machine would read whatever memory sits below the stack.
attacks.detail: main[0] ADD: operand stack underflow (the instruction needs a value but the stack is empty)

attacks.attack: Inconsistent stack depth at a merge point
attacks.why: Two paths reach the same instruction with different stack depths, so the machine cannot know what is on the stack there. This is the property that makes bytecode verification possible at all.
attacks.detail:
main[5] PRINT: operand stack underflow (the instruction needs a value but the stack is empty)
      main: instruction 5 is reached with stack depth 0 on one path and 1 on another - the operand stack is not consistent at this merge point

attacks.why: A string is multiplied by an integer. If the machine simply trusted the opcode, the string's internal pointer would be used as a number - the classic route to arbitrary memory access.
attacks.detail: main[2] MUL: arithmetic on a string value

attacks.why: Slot 1 is read before anything is ever written to it, which leaks whatever the previous call left in that stack slot.
attacks.detail: main[0] LOAD: local slot 1 is read before it is ever written

attacks.why: LOAD addresses slot 40 in a frame that only has 2 slots, reaching into the caller's frame or past the end of the stack entirely.
attacks.detail: main[0] LOAD: slot 40 is outside the activation record (0..1)

attacks.attack: Denial of service: a loop that never ends
attacks.why: This bytecode is perfectly type-safe and passes every static check. Nothing static can prove it terminates, so the *sandbox* has to stop it with an instruction budget.
attacks.detail: sandbox stopped the program: instruction budget of 200000 exhausted - the program does not terminate

attacks.why: Also statically valid. The sandbox caps the number of activation records, so the machine reports a policy violation instead of exhausting memory.
attacks.detail: sandbox stopped the program: call depth limit of 64 reached - runaway recursion in 'boom'

nonterminating_live.error: sandbox stopped the program: instruction budget of 250000 exhausted - the program does not terminate

nonterminating_run.error: sandbox stopped the program: instruction budget of 2000000 exhausted - the program does not terminate
